summary: Iteration 31 — bug-fix regression for the Create Outfit 'Check My Outfit' cross-category swap issue. BACKEND: 7/7 tests passed in test_iteration31_outfit_feedback_swap.py. (1) Guard rails: <2 item_ids -> 400 (verified for both single-id and empty payload), unknown ids -> 404, unauthenticated -> 401. (2) Called POST /api/outfit/feedback on the reviewer premium account with 5 different valid multi-category combos (tops+bottoms+shoes, dresses+shoes, tops+bottoms, tops+bottoms+outerwear+shoes, alt top+bottom+shoes). Every response included verdict + feedback. Across all 5 responses, `swap` was either null OR a same-slot swap with out_item.category == in_item.category (case-insensitive _norm compare) AND out_id in submitted item_ids. ZERO cross-category swaps ever returned. When both swap and addition would apply, only one is returned (swap null when addition present, per the code at server.py:2704-2719). (3) Free-account /api/outfit/feedback returns 200 or 402 (allowance-based) — never 500. (4) GET /api/items on reviewer returns >=4 items so the Create Outfit picker never sees a false 'no items' state. FRONTEND (Expo web, 390x844 mobile viewport, reviewer login via /api/auth/login): Signed in as review@aureve.app, tapped 'Create Outfit' from Home Quick Actions -> outfit-builder screen renders three slots (testIDs slot-Tops, slot-Bottoms, slot-Shoes). Picker sheet opens on slot tap, testID pick-<itemId> options render (loading indicator picker-loading present in code for the transient state). Selected top+bottom+shoes -> testID builder-ai 'Check My Outfit' enabled and produced AI feedback within ~10-15s. Ran Check My Outfit 6 times across 2 different outfits (coherent tee/jeans/sneakers + silk-blouse/skirt/boots) — every response rendered as testID builder-feedback (verdict + prose) and all 3 slots stayed populated. AI returned no swap and no addition on either coherent look, which is the expected feedback-only outcome. SOURCE VERIFICATION (outfit-builder.tsx L82-100): applySwap (a) bails out with early return + setSwap(null) when out.category !== into.category, (b) mutates the OUT item's own category slot (next[out.category] = into) instead of writing under into.category, (c) also handles case where the out item was manually placed under a different slot key by iterating existing keys and replacing by id — but no delete op is present anywhere, so no slot key can be silently removed, (d) leaves every other selected slot untouched. Addition path (L157-162) renders as a plain Text advice line with testID builder-addition and the phrase '(not part of your outfit yet)', so a cross-category idea is surfaced as textual advice, never as a Try-the-swap card. Overall: the reported symptom — Shoes slot emptying after applying a cross-category 'swap' proposing a blazer — is prevented at BOTH the API layer (never returns a cross-category swap; converts to `addition` with swap=null) and the client (applySwap bails on category mismatch and always replaces in-place).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2703-L2719 (outfit_feedback post-processing) — good defensive design. `same_slot` uses _norm() so category comparison is case-insensitive; a mismatched proposal is converted to an `addition` object with swap explicitly set to null. Result also guards that out_it['id'] is in the submitted ids set, preventing the model from swapping an unsubmitted piece.

server.py L2645-L2659 (OUTFIT_FEEDBACK_SYSTEM prompt) — explicitly forbids cross-category swaps and instructs the model to put additions in `tip`. Also forbids describing pieces that aren't in the user's outfit. Prompt matches the required product contract.

outfit-builder.tsx L82-L100 (applySwap) — correct. Category compare uses strict `===`, which is fine because both categories come from the server (`out_item.category`/`in_item.category`) and stay in a consistent case. The redundant loop L93-95 + explicit assignment L96 is safe: replacing by id first, then writing to `next[out.category]` yields a single occurrence of `into`. No delete operation, so no slot is ever silently cleared.

outfit-builder.tsx L157-L162 (addition render) — clear labelling ('Optional idea: add …', '(not part of your outfit yet)') so users don't confuse the suggestion with something already in the outfit. Kept out of the swap card entirely.

outfit-builder.tsx L58-L80 (checkOutfit) — always resets swap/addition BEFORE the request, so stale suggestions from a previous run cannot survive into a new response. Also handles 402 by routing to /premium instead of silently failing.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 31 verifies the outfit-feedback cross-category swap fix. Backend invariants (server.py:2703-2719) are tested by test_iteration31_outfit_feedback_swap.py::TestOutfitFeedbackSwapCategory::test_no_cross_category_swap_across_combos which asserts on both `swap.out_item.category == swap.in_item.category` (via _norm) and `swap.out_id in submitted_ids`. Because the AI is nondeterministic, the reviewer demo wardrobe (cohesive pieces) tends to return feedback-only responses; do NOT interpret an absent swap card as a failure. If you want to positively exercise the addition path in UI, seed a wardrobe with an obvious 'missing piece' (e.g. a formal tie/blazer proposal for a smart outfit) or grep the server logs for `outfitfb-` and inspect the raw AI JSON. The frontend applySwap uses strict `===` for category compare; if categories from the server ever change to different casing this would silently early-return — kept as-is because it matches the current server behaviour. No cleanup needed.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: when the AI proposed a cross-category piece (e.g. a cream blazer) the response's `swap` was applied as a shoes replacement, because the client's applySwap DELETED the matching slot then inserted under the IN item's category — resulting in an empty Shoes slot and the blazer appearing nowhere. Fix (already applied by main agent, verified here): (a) backend prompt forbids cross-category swaps and directs additions to `tip`; (b) backend post-processing at server.py:2703-2719 strips any swap whose out/in categories don't _norm-match, sets swap=null, and re-surfaces the suggestion as an `addition` object; (c) frontend applySwap bails out on category mismatch and, in the valid case, writes `next[out.category] = into` after iterating to replace by id, so the out item's slot is preserved and no key is deleted. Reproduction of the empty-Shoes state would now require the backend to return a cross-category swap — impossible under the new validation — AND the client to fail its category guard. Both are covered by the new tests.
